Although deep learning frameworks are abundant, they predominantly lack scalability and adaptability for diverse model architectures and data types. To address these limitations, we introduce MMLSpark, an extensible, scalable, and flexible deep learning framework built upon Apache Spark and designed to facilitate easy creation of novel networks. Validated against Criteo competition benchmarks, MMLspark achieves performance matching or surpassing that of MNetspark within a fraction of time. Furthermore, its inherent modularity allows users to readily develop new models tailored to specific data requirements.

Translation between spoken languages presents a difficult task due to the need to convert audio from one language into another while significantly altering acoustic characteristics and phonetic structures. While existing research predominantly addresses speech-to-speech translation between different languages, it often overlooks the characteristics of the target language or the acoustic profile of the source language. We introduce a new zero-shot translation approach that utilizes speech synthesis combined with text-based autoencoders capable of zero-shot training. Our model successfully integrates features such as language style, content, and acoustics from the source and content phrases, while employing a shift in the codebook space to capture language style. Evaluation results indicate that models trained on only one language outperform current state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both acoustic and phonetic quality.

This article introduces a general Coleman-Gorton system with temporal and spatial parameters. We demonstrate the existence and uniqueness of a global strong solution. The analysis draws from a generic framework for general nonlinear parabolic equations featuring sufficiently monotonic properties. This result, in turn, allows for the derivation of existence and uniqueness solutions within specific cases.

This paper introduces a probabilistic load forecasting methodology specifically designed to handle the variable and spatially distinct load patterns of individual households. A key challenge addressed here is that while probablistic forecasting can reveal load variations, its efficacy diminishes within a short-term horizon due to the convergence of prediction uncertainty with actual load variability of household devices. To mitigate this, an initial section outlines the methodology for estimating the temporal characteristic curves of devices. Building on this, a prediction model is developed to forecast the load profile of devices, incorporating both mean values and uncertainty data derived from the first step. Finally, these device-level forecasts are aggregated to estimate the total household load probability distribution. An analysis demonstrates that merging short-term forecasts from different models significantly reduces overall prediction uncertainty. Furthermore, the study confirms that the probability distribution effectively characterizes load peaks, revealing that peak load uncertainty is consistently lower than the uncertainty surrounding the peak load value itself.

While domains like biology and finance are increasingly leveraging machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance decision-making and operational efficiency, a persistent obstacle remains the scarcity of domain-specific context within ML-driven models. This gap complicates the accurate interpretation of outcomes, hinders the generalization and efficacy of these systems as they tackle evolving challenges within their fields, and ultimately restricts the seamless adoption of AI-driven tools by stakeholders and end-users. To address this hurdle, this paper offers an initial framework aimed at guiding the incorporation of domain expertise during the ML model development lifecycle, facilitating future progress toward full integration. To make this feasible, we have established two primary principles: the explicit identification of the critical data and knowledge sources necessary for model construction and the methodology for embedding this domain expertise directly into algorithms and neural network architectures to ensure better alignment with disciplinary nuances. This approach also serves as a foundation for the intentional engineering and deployment of explainable AI (XAI) systems that seamlessly fuse domain insights with machine learning. Consequently, we anticipate producing an online resource dedicated to scoping these domain-specific assets and advancing the advancement of such integrated systems.

The emergence of the COVID-19 virus has accelerated the demand for effective diagnostic tools to assist healthcare professionals. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have become integral to diagnosing the infection via CT pulmonary lesion localization and segmentation, which utilize lung opacities as indicators. However, fully automatic methods depend on large, meticulously annotated datasets that are impractical to gather during pandemic crises. To address this, we introduce a novel, cost-effective framework for training unbiased lesion localization models using only unannotated images and a set of positively classified samples within the detection phase. This approach, termed ULBL-C (Unbiased Lesion Localization with Co-training), leverages UNL (Unsupervised Node Learning) and Co-trainer strategies by training two distinct models on different feature spaces and integrating their agreement during training via consensus. Additionally, an internal consistency loss is applied to leverage correlations among neighboring pixels at the supervisory unsupervised level, enhancing segmentation performance. Experiments conducted on two major COVID-19 datasets validate this proposed framework.

Accurate localization and identification of vertebrae in CT images are essential for diagnosing and treating spinal diseases. Unlike automated methods, interaction with a radiologist can mitigate identification inaccurities; specifically, guiding misidentified or misplaced results often yields better performance than the system's unassisted output alone. This paper demonstrates that the traditional approach of correcting spinal vertebrae based on their anatomical constraints—such as consistent size, spacing, orientation, alignment, symmetry, and boundary with the brainstem—is effective. We propose a unified localization and identification framework that begins with CT vertebrae segmentation, followed by identification through anatomically constrained optimization of vertebra centroids and endplates. A location model respecting spinal geometry enhances localization quality; consequently, interaction allows radiologists to guide localization where the CT features are ambiguous. Furthermore, identification is refined as it corrects localization errors while adhering to constraints. Experimental findings indicate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.935 in CT datasets from a private institution, and an accuracy of 0.817 according to a public dataset from the University of Chicago Medical Center.

This work examines the dynamical stabilization of a scattering electron through time-dependent quantum fluctuations of the vacuum. Due to the finite lifetime associated with the interaction, this phenomenon is inherently transient in nature and thus distinct from time-independent stabilization achieved through strong fields. We investigate how this effect manifests when strong-laser-driven electrons interact with the metallic surface of a shell-type cavity, a scenario that allows us to analyze how the temporal scale of light-matter coupling influences the scattering cross-section. Our findings demonstrate that dynamical stabilization can emerge within sub-cycle light-matter interaction windows if a strong field excites surface plasmons. Additionally, we identify a specific regime where this stabilization becomes unobservable because the strong field profoundly alters the cavity's structure, effectively transforming it into a slab configuration. Finally, we propose experimental techniques capable of probing these effects by utilizing attosecond pulses to excite the surface plasmons rather than directly driving the incoming electrons, a method suitable for present-day experimental setups.

While electric actuators are standard in modern quadruped locomotion, they are stiff and lack the elastic properties necessary for locomotion based on nonlinear dynamics or inverted pendulum strategies like Capture Point (CP) flat-footedness. Although elastic elements are well-understood for generating nonholonomic, energy-saving strides, their application to rigid gait patterns remains largely unexplored. This study investigates elastic actuation for both conservative and non-conservative quadrupedal walking, aiming to simplify control input requirements compared to traditional high-end electric motors. Specifically, the research explores the feasibility of elastic performance within standard holonomic paces, demonstrating through simulation and analytical comparison the advantages of elasticity in reducing control variables and power draw. The simulations confirm significant potential advantages for elasticity in conventional walking cycles, suggesting comparable efficiency and reduced operational constraints when applied even to non-conservative, electric-compatible loops.

We introduce a direct approach to address the problem of separability in quantum mechanics, rooted in the quantum energy infimum (QEI)—a novel concept defined here—and the ensuing variational principle derived from it. Although the energy QEI is defined broadly, the principle's applications to the four-pronged bipartite entangled systems of two quantum levels are examined, utilizing numerical estimates against analytical QEI values.

In collisionless plasmas featuring a sheet-like charge separation field perpendicular to the dominant particle flow, it is established that an instability arises within a limited region parallel to the flow, situated upstream and inside the initial beam plasma density. While this phenomenon was previously identified numerically as a growth mechanism for magnetic fields by Drakakis et al. (2017), the  the underlying  physics  remains undefined. Using non-linear particle-in-cell simulations, we characterize this instability, demonstrating that it stems from resonating magnetic cyclotron motion of downstream and upstream particles interacting with a magnetic whistler wave. Furthermore, we determine that this mode operates a mechanism that transfers parallel momentum into transverse momentum via the generation of magnetic and wave energy alongside plasma turbulence as it develops through nonlinear stages. It appears likely to play a significant role in the dynamics of astrophysical plasmas characterized by strong magnetic fields.

Traditional trait manipulation (TP) in fashion design often relies on labor-intensive, expert-driven techniques. Recent advancements in computer vision have introduced automatic image-based TP methods; however, they frequently generate suboptinal results stemming from layout issues, inappropriate color choices, and flawed material assignments. Addressing these shortcomings, we present a novel approach for Semi-supervised Feature-level Trait Manipulation (SFLTM) aimed at enhancing automatic TP, specifically for fashion retrieval. Our method decomposes input garment images into distinct trait layers, encouraging proper layer-wise segmentation, and employs clustering to discover an extensive dataset of inherited traits. By integrating these features with a clustering strategy, we construct a comprehensive trait library. Furthermore, we define an optimal feature-level manipulation objective that jointly ensures accurate trait selection and effective instance re-ranking. Experimental results on a prominent benchmark demonstrate that SFLTM outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in both automatic trait manipulation and fashion retrieval tasks. Notable successes achieved include the winning submissions to the Trait Manipulation Challenge within the IEEE CVPR Fashion IAI Competition 2021, as well as winning entries to both the Microblading Challenge and Stylist Challenge under CVFER 2021.

This work investigates a dual gradient method designed to resolve linear ill-posed equations. Specifically, it examines cases featuring linear operators mapping from a Banach space $X$ to a Hilbert space $Y$ with closed range. The study examines the method's convergence behavior across both noise-free scenarios and cases where data contains noise. Ultimately, it demonstrates that the dual gradient method adheres to a filtered reverse strategy, encompassing a convergence rate that extends beyond traditional rates often seen in filtered back projection methods.

Traditionally, this step involves comparing similar sub-apertures, which can be intensified when blocks are small. To mitigate these computational burdens, we suggest an efficient, lookup-integrated cost volume builder designed specifically for depth estimation within light field processing. Furthermore, our strategy keeps track of potential occlusions throughout the calculator using regional datasets to speed up volume construction and enhance overall precision. Empirical results indicate superior performance in restoring occluded light fields compared to established methodologies across diverse testing scenarios under variable daylight conditions.

Under densely populated environments, sustaining high quality of service in home networks demands efficient allocation of radio resources to mitigate interference and channel congestion. This paper introduces a two-phase framework, utilizing an IEEE 802.11 standard-based protocol, to enhance the association of access points (APs) and extenders within residential settings. In the initial phase, the system estimates the current AP or extender load by analyzing delayed reporting fields within the 802.11s protocol; the phase followed by an intelligent selection algorithm that guides client devices toward the optimal connection based on channel load and channel quality metrics. The methodology incorporates advanced features such as IEEE 802.11n for improved performance and reliability. Simulation results indicate that the proposed scheme is effective, particularly in dense deployments, and demonstrates the capability to balance network loads. The entire approach is implemented in OpenWet distribution as an OpenWet firmware module.
